title: Explain Then Check
user: Technical self-learners who can recognize flashcards but need short, deliberate practice explaining a concept, mechanism, and trade-off in their own words.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A learner of system design and distributed systems asks whether spaced repetition helps with deep understanding; respondents emphasize building and practicing concepts.
A learner describes repeatedly pressing Again without learning the crucial distinction and asks how to avoid brute-force repetition.

recurrence: Independent learners in technical and language domains report the same recognition-versus-understanding gap; the severity is wasted review time and false confidence.
current_workaround: Write free-form notes, explain aloud with no record, make more cards, or rely on a chatbot to ask improvised questions.
incumbents_and_gap: Anki optimizes recall intervals; RemNote and chat tutors collect notes or converse. None makes a 90-second structured explanation with self-selected omissions and later retry the smallest unit.
smallest_useful_product: A local prompt runner: choose a concept, record or type an explanation under headings (what, why, failure case), mark missing pieces, and schedule only those missing pieces for another attempt.
success_measure: At least half of weekly active users retry five or more marked omissions within seven days, and 70% mark a retry clearer than its first attempt.
constraints: Audio remains on device by default; no automated claim that an explanation is correct; support export/delete.
why_distinct: It trains generative explanation without pretending an LLM can certify understanding.
